A New York jury has found Chinese telecom giant Huawei guilty of stealing trade secrets and other criminal offences, but acquitted it of a racketeering conspiracy and obstruction of justice. Real Madrid extended their winning run to 10 games in all competitions on Tuesday, overturning an early deficit to rout PSV Eindhoven 5-1 in the Champions League, with Jude Bellingham scoring a spectacular goal and Kylian Mbappé netting twice. On Nov. 24, 1947, the U.S. Navy launched the first Aerobee rocket into the sky, but it never reached space.

Aerobee was a suborbital sounding rocket designed to study Earth's atmosphere.

After World War 2, the United States started reusing erman V-2 rockets for this kind of research. When they started running out of V-2 rockets, the United States constructed its own rockets that were similar but cheaper to build and to launch. In the weeks leading up to the first Aerobee mission, three test flights were launched.

Those tests used a dummy version of Aerobee with a live booster to see if the two stages would separate properly. On Aerobee's first real flight, the rocket flew about 35 miles high. That's below the 62-mile (100 kilometers) upper limit for the boundary of space. (NASA and the U.S. military typically consider 50 miles the edge of space.) Mission control cut the flight short after about 30 seconds, because Aerobee started to yaw, and they wanted to keep it from going completely out of control.

Why it mattered

Billed as the "most successful sounding rocket of the space age," the initial Aerobee rocket was suborbital rocket designed to launch experment payload of up to 100 pounds (45 kilograms) to an altitude of 75 miles (121 kilometers) or so.

"The Aerobee was designed to carry instruments aloft to collect data on the upper atmosphere and to place small animals in a weightless condition for physiological studies," the U.S. National Museum of the United States Air Force wrote in a mission overview. "It was launched by a solid-propellant booster engine of 18,000 pounds thrust that burned for only two and a half seconds."

While the first Aerobee rocket did not reach space, many more made successful launches in the decades that followed.

Engineers made a steady stream of upgrades to the the Aerobee rocket, allowing to fly higher and launch heavier payloads into space. It was an Aerobee rocket that launched two Phillipine monkeys on a mission to study how the effects of rapid launch acceleration might affect their bodies, an experiment that was among the frst human physiology tests that paved the way for human spaceflight.

More than 1,000 Aerobee rockets have launched since then, and the last one flew in January of 1985.

]]> <![CDATA[ 1st-ever detection of a dying star's 'final nuclear heartbeat' challenges what we know about our sun's eventual death ]]> As ubiquitous as the sun is to us today, our star is not eternal; one day, albeit in billions of years, it will die. While massive stars die in supernova explosions, the sun and stars of similar mass die quieter deaths. But that doesn't mean these stars completely go out with a whimper.

New observations collected using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), the world's largest radio telescope comprised of 66 antennas in northern Chile, reveal that the sun's death throes may be different from what scientists had initially believed.

NASA Jet Propulsion Lab (JPL) researcher Raghvendra Sahai, who led the investigation, explained the shape the ALMA observations took: "It's essentially a physical snapshot of an event that, until now, we've mostly inferred from theoretical models. We've caught, for the first time, a star's final nuclear heartbeat, frozen in gas."

Sun-like stars "die" when they run out of hydrogen in their cores. This means that the fusion of hydrogen to helium ceases in the stellar core, and because this nuclear process is a star's main energy source, the star no longer has the outward push to support itself against the inward push of its own gravity.

As the star's core collapses to create a stellar remnant called a white dwarf, the outer layers where hydrogen is still fusing to form helium swell out. This expansion leads to a relatively short-lived "red giant" phase. Eventually, these outer layers will cool and disperse, leaving the central white dwarf surrounded by a so-called "planetary nebula" shell of debris.

During the red giant phase, as the stellar core is surrounded by shells of hydrogen and helium, these layers are occasionally rocked by flares in nuclear activity called thermal pulses. During these episodes, stellar material is flung into space.

To better understand this phase in stellar evolution, the team focused ALMA on a star called IRAS 06530-0213, located around 12,000 light-years away in the constellation Monoceros. This revealed a giant ring of gas that appears to be a frozen fossil of the star's last thermonuclear flare-up. This thermonuclear fossil rings an hourglass-shaped planetary nebula in the act of forming.

"Most of us think of stars as unchanging points of light, but this is a real-time snapshot of a star's death throes," Sahai said. "It's the brief, violent transition between a bloated red giant and a glowing planetary nebula, frozen mid-action."

The team was able to determine that this gas shell of IRAS 06530-0213 is around half a light-year wide and was ejected into space around 6,500 years ago. It represents the first direct evidence of the last thermal pulse before this kind of star enters the final phase of its life.

The team thinks that for around 2,000 years after the pulse, the star lost mass at a lower rate. This mass loss then increased sharply over the following 1,000 years. This led to the creation of a lumpy shell of gas now seen as a tangle of material filaments around the dying star. The fact that these filaments have a spiral shape could indicate that IRAS 06530-0213 has an unseen partner orbiting it, stirring the gas.

Meanwhile, the hourglass-shaped nebula immediately around the star began to take shape around 700 years ago, meaning that the red giant phase for IRAS 06530-0213 only ended very recently, in cosmic terms at least.

There are also unexpected elements to the ALMA observations of IRAS 06530-0213.

Strange chemistry of dying star

The team discovered an unexpected abundance of heavy versions, or isotopes, of elements like carbon, oxygen and nitrogen around IRAS 06530-0213.

This doesn't conform to models of how stars like IRAS 06530-0213 forge elements and mix them into their surroundings, though similar signatures have been seen around odd stellar objects, with violent bursts of nuclear fusion thought to be the cause.

As well as seeing something unexpected, the researchers didn't detect something they expected to observe.

Dying stars like IRAS 06530-0213 have previously been known to have companions, typically sitting with them inside compact disks of dust. These disks are indirect evidence of material being dragged from the close companion star to the dying star. This is a process scientists have used to explain jet-sculpted hourglass shapes.

However, ALMA failed to detect such disk around IRAS 06530. The team suggests that this could be because a disk existed, albeit briefly, during which time it powered a short burst of high-speed jets that helped sculpt the hourglass, following this the disk simply faded away.

"Dying stars so often have hidden companions that reshape their ejected material into intricate, bipolar or multipolar forms instead of simple spheres," Sahai concluded. "IRAS 06530 shows that the story is more complicated than the tidy explanation we've been using."

The team's research was published on Friday (Nov. 20) in The Astrophysical Journal.

A spacecraft far from Earth beamed home a rare sight: a solar eclipse caused by one asteroid casting its shadow on another.

What is it?

The image shows the Didymos double asteroid system, which consists of the larger Didymos and its moonlet, Dimorphos. In this image, Dimorphos' shadow can be seen on the surface of Didymos.

The image was captured by the European Space Agency's (ESA's) Hera probe, which was sent to rendezvous with Didymos. Once there, Hera's job is to inspect the system to study the aftermath of NASA's historic DART mission (Double Asteroid Redirect Test), which slammed a kinetic impactor into Dimorphos in September 2022 in an attempt to alter its orbit and thus the trajectory of the entire two-asteroid system.

Such missions, should they ever be needed in the future, could potentially redirect an asteroid on a collision course with Earth.

Why is it incredible?

For one, this image is incredible given that it was beamed home by Hera while it approaches Didymos some 121 million miles (195 million kilometers) away from Earth.

But more than that, this image reveals incredible details of the Didymos system. Scientists call Didymos a "rubble pile" asteroid, meaning it's a loose body made up of boulders, dust, gravel and other bits of the solar system held together by the asteroid's own gravity. In the image, many of these irregular boulders and rocks can be seen strewn across Didymos and its moonlet.

Hera will reach the system on Nov. 25, and ESA will release the first full images from the mission.

]]> <![CDATA[ China's Shenzhou-24 mission launches 1st international astronaut to Tiangong space station ]]>

China has launed an international astronaut to its Tiangong space station today (Nov. 24) for the first time ever, marking a significant milestone for international participation in the Chinese space program.

A Long March 2F rocket lifted off with the Shenzhou-24 crew from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China today at 7:18 p.m. EST (0018 GMT and 8:18 a.m. Beijing time on Nov. 25).

You can watch the liftoff live here at Space.com, courtesy of China Central Television (CCTV).

Shenzhou-24 is China's 18th crewed spaceflight to date and its 12th astronaut mission to Tiangong, a three-module station that the nation finished assembling in low Earth orbit in late 2022.

Those numbers may sound rather prosaic. But today's flight makes history, marking the first time that China has ever launched a foreign national to space. That trailblazer is Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a former pilot in Pakistan's armed forces who is the first person from his country ever to reach orbit. (Adventurer Namira Salim is the first Pakistani ever to fly to the final frontier, doing so on a Virgin Galactic suborbital mission in October 2023.)

China and Pakistan began paving Ali's path to Tiangong in February 2025, with the signing of a spaceflight cooperation agreement in Islamabad. Pakistan then selected two astronaut candidates, who traveled to China for training.

We didn't learn which Pakistani astronaut was picked for Shenzhou-24 until Monday night (Nov. 23), when China announced the mission's crew. This is not out of the ordinary, by the way; China generally doesn't reveal the identity of Shenzhou astronauts until the day before launch.

This is in keeping with the nation's broader spaceflight ethos, which prizes keeping things close to the vest.

Ali is flying as a payload specialist. The other Shenzhou-24 astronauts are commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer ​Wu Yi. Tang also flew on the Shenzhou-12 and Shenzhou-17 missions, which launched in June 2021 and October 2023, respectively. He will be the first person to visit Tiangong three times, according to the state-run Xinhua news agency. Shenzhou-24 will be the first spaceflight for Wu.

Tang and Wu are expected to live aboard Tiangong for six months, the usual Shenzhou rotation. But Ali will stay in orbit for just a week or so, coming back down to Earth with Zhang Zhiyuan and Lai Ka-ying of the Shenzhou-23 mission, which launched on May 24.

According to the South China Morning Post, the third Shenzhou-23 crewmate, Zhu Yangzhu, will stay behind when Ali leaves, living aboard Tiangong until Shenzhou-24 comes home. Zhu will therefore become the first Chinese astronaut ever to spend a year in orbit, a milestone that will allow China to prep for long-duration missions to the moon and other deep-space locales.

]]> <![CDATA[ Russia launches Progress 97 cargo ship to the International Space Station (video) ]]>

Russia's latest freighter is on its way to the International Space Station.

The robotic Progress 97 cargo craft launched atop a Soyuz rocket from the Russia-run Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan today (Nov. 24) at 5:17 a.m. EST (1013 GMT; 3:17 p.m. Baikonur time), carrying several tons of supplies for the astronauts aboard the orbiting lab.

If all goes to plan, Progress 97 will arrive at the International Space Station (ISS) on Thursday (Nov. 26), docking with its Poisk module. But the freighter won't stay at that particular locale for long.

The cosmonauts currently living on the ISS — Pyotr Dubrov, Anna Kikina and Sergey Teteryatnikov — will unload Progress 97 through Poisk. But the freighter will then hop over to a different port, according to journalist and space historian Anatoly Zak: the aft one of the PrK transfer tunnel, which leads to Russia's Zvezda service module.

The PrK port is the best site for engine burns that boost the orbit of the ISS, a service that Progress freighters regularly provide. But Progress 97 cannot unload its cargo through that port because the PrK transfer tunnel has been sealed off, due to an ongoing air leak that was first documented in 2019.

Progress-97 is therefore "the first cargo mission scheduled to unload its cargo and perform orbit corrections of the ISS at different docking ports," Zak wrote on the site he runs, RussianSpaceWeb.com.

The Progress 97 mission, which Russia calls Progress MS-36, was originally expected to launch this past August, according to Zak. But the liftoff was pushed back several times, most significantly by the collapse of the service platform at Baikonur's Site 31 in November 2025. It took Russia about three months to repair the platform, leading to a series of delays.

Progress 97 will likely stay docked to the ISS for about six months, after which it will be loaded up with trash and sent home to burn up in Earth's atmosphere.

Japan's HTV-X vehicle and Northrop Grumman's Cygnus spacecraft are similarly expendable. The only currently operational ISS cargo craft that's reusable is SpaceX's Dragon capsule, which makes parachute-aided ocean splashdowns at the end of its missions.

 <description>Dvacet let mohli Slováci žijící v zahraničí hlasovat v parlamentních volbách poštou. Od příštích voleb už budou muset osobně na ambasádu nebo konzulát.  <description>Polský vzdušný prostor narušil v noci na úterý ruský průzkumný dron s kamerami. Agresor ho napadl při zásahu u Kauflandu</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/906586-utok-na-straznika-v-jablonci-agresor-ho-napadl-pri-zasahu-u-kauflandu.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/906586-utok-na-straznika-v-jablonci-agresor-ho-napadl-pri-zasahu-u-kauflandu.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 24 Nov 2026 18:45:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>Strážníci městské policie v Jablonci nad Nisou museli v pátek řešit nejen zraněného muže před prodejnou Kaufland, ale také agresivního kolemjdoucího, který hlídku slovně napadal, odmítal uposlechnout výzvy, a nakonec jednoho ze strážníků fyzicky napadl.</description></item><item><title>Minulý týden zmizela. Po ženě z Jablonce pátrá policie</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/906611-minuly-tyden-zmizela-po-zene-z-jablonce-patra-policie.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/906611-minuly-tyden-zmizela-po-zene-z-jablonce-patra-policie.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 24 Nov 2026 16:45:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>Jablonečtí policisté pátrají po devětačtyřicetileté ženě z Jablonce. Ta minulý týden odešla z domova a od té doby je nezvěstná. Její pohřešování ohlásil v pondělí její přítel.</description></item><item><title>Oprava tramvajové trati k nádraží v Liberci bude asi výrazně levnější</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/906579-oprava-trate-k-nadrazi-v-liberci-bude-asi-vyrazne-levnejsi-prace-zacnou-po.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/906579-oprava-trate-k-nadrazi-v-liberci-bude-asi-vyrazne-levnejsi-prace-zacnou-po.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 24 Nov 2026 16:00:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Doprava</category><description>Oprava tramvajové tratě z dolního centra k vlakovému nádraží v Liberci bude asi výrazně levnější, než městský dopravní podnik (DPMLJ) očekával. Práce nejspíš začnou příští rok po zimě.</description></item><item><title>Tankujete v Polsku do kanystrů? Celníci vám je mohou zabavit, ani účtenka nepomůže</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906577-tankujete-v-polsku-do-kanystru-celnici-vam-je-mohou-zabavit-ani-uctenka-nepomuze.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906577-tankujete-v-polsku-do-kanystru-celnici-vam-je-mohou-zabavit-ani-uctenka-nepomuze.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 24 Nov 2026 14:03:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Převážíte benzin v kanystrech ze zahraničí? Liberečtí celníci varují před překračováním zákonných limitů pro osobní spotřebu. Při nedávné kontrole odhalili 120 litrů paliva a od začátku roku zabavili už 1350 litrů nelegálně převážených pohonných hmot.</description></item><item><title>Podzimní sbírka zajistila pro potřebné v Libereckém kraji přes 36 tun zboží</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906549-podzimni-sbirka-zajistila-pro-potrebne-v-libereckem-kraji-pres-36-tun-zbozi.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906549-podzimni-sbirka-zajistila-pro-potrebne-v-libereckem-kraji-pres-36-tun-zbozi.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 24 Nov 2026 12:45:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Rekordních bezmála 36,5 tuny trvanlivých potravin, drogerie a hygienických potřeb zajistilo Potravinové bance Libereckého kraje podzimní kolo veřejné sbírky. Je to zhruba o čtyři tuny víc než loni, prázdné sklady se díky tomu naplnily, řekl ředitel liberecké potravinové banky Josef Vlček.</description></item><item><title>Policisté hledají cestující z autobusu, ve kterém upadla starší žena</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/906555-policiste-hledaji-cestujici-z-autobusu-ve-kterem-upadla-starsi-zena.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/906555-policiste-hledaji-cestujici-z-autobusu-ve-kterem-upadla-starsi-zena.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 24 Nov 2026 10:54:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>Policisté pátrají po svědcích události, ke které došlo už 2. června v Horním Vítkově, kde se při pádu v autobusu zranila starší žena.</description></item><item><title>Velké skiareály v Libereckém kraji spustily díky ochlazení zasněžování</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/906520-velke-skiarealy-v-libereckem-kraji-diky-ochlazeni-spustily-zasnezovaci.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/906520-velke-skiarealy-v-libereckem-kraji-diky-ochlazeni-spustily-zasnezovaci.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 24 Nov 2026 08:59:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Fotbal</category><description>Velké skiareály v Libereckém kraji díky ochlazení mohly spustit běžné zasněžovací systémy, které potřebují teploty pod bodem mrazu. Slibný je i výhled počasí pro další dny, řekl ředitel společnosti Ski bižu Pavel Bažant, která provozuje dva největší skiareály v Jizerských horách.</description></item><item><title>Lidé rozhodli: V Liberci vzniknou za 10 milionů nové parky i obří mural</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906532-lide-rozhodli-v-liberci-vzniknou-za-10-milionu-nove-parky-i-obri-mural.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906532-lide-rozhodli-v-liberci-vzniknou-za-10-milionu-nove-parky-i-obri-mural.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 24 Nov 2026 06:33:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Obyvatelé Liberce opět promluvili do podoby svého města. V hlasování participativního rozpočtu Tvoříme Liberec 2026 rozdělili téměř šest tisíc hlasů a vybrali devět vítězných projektů. V následujících dvou letech se tak město dočká obnovy rybníčků, lesní jógové stezky nebo nových odpočinkových zón.</description></item><item><title>Srážka dodávky a kamionu v Provodíně. Vrtulník transportoval zraněného do nemocnice</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/906526-srazka-dodavky-a-kamionu-v-provodine-vrtulnik-transportoval-zraneneho-do-nemocnice.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/906526-srazka-dodavky-a-kamionu-v-provodine-vrtulnik-transportoval-zraneneho-do-nemocnice.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 20:09:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Doprava</category><description>K nehodě dodávky a nákladního auta v Provodíně na Českolipsku vyjížděly dnes ve 12:13 dvě jednotky profesionálních hasičů. Ze zdemolované dodávky museli vyprostit zaklíněného člověka, kterého následně letecká záchranná služba přepravila do libereckého traumacentra.</description></item></channel></rss>

výběžek.eu https://www.vybezek.eu dobrý den ze šluknovského výběžku, konce světa - šluknovský výběžek Tue, 24 Nov 2026 16:25:31 +0000 cs hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=7.1.5 https://www.vybezek.eu/wp-uploads/2018/09/cropped-favicon-vybezek-32x32.png výběžek.eu https://www.vybezek.eu 32 32 Ezagutu Lužice aneb Poznejte Lužici https://www.vybezek.eu/297720-ezagutu-luzice-aneb-poznejte-luzici/ Mon, 23 Nov 2026 18:23:04 +0000 https://www.vybezek.eu/?p=297720 Literárně naučné miniturné po Čechách lužickosrbské spisovatelky Róži Domašcyny, básníka a překladatele Milana Hrabala a hudebníka Vojtěcha Kouby.

Ve dnech 3. a 4. listopadu 2026 proběhly dva večery věnované lužickosrbské literatuře a kultuře pod názvem Ezagutu Lužice (Poznejte Lužici), které pořádaly, ruku v ruce, nakladatelství Euskaldun a Společnost přátel Lužice. Nejednalo se o první takovou spolupráci, ale o vyvrcholení celého cyklu pořadů věnovaným menším jazykovým skupinám bez vlastní státnosti, které jsou nějakým způsobem svázány s českými zeměmi. První večer proběhl v Plzni v univerzitní kavárně Družba a následující den se přesunul takříkajíc na domácí hřiště do pražského Lužického semináře.

Hlavními hvězdami večerů byly Róža Domašcyna, jedna z nejvýznamnějších lužickosrbských autorek a Milan Hrabal, básník, překladatel, přítel a propagátor Lužice. O hudební doprovod se postaral Vojtěch Kouba, který představil publiku lužický folklór, ale zároveň i vlastní tvorbu.

Na první večer dorazilo asi čtyřicet zvídavých Plzeňanů, pro které bylo setkání s literaturou a historií nejmenšího západoslovanského národa iniciačním zážitkem. Milan Hrabal se ukázal, jako výborný průvodce lužicko-srbskými reáliemi i historií. Navíc bavil publikum tím, jak se postupně přiznával k různým překladatelským přehmatům. Poezie Róži Domašcyny a písně Vojtěcha Kouby vykouzlily čarovnou atmosféru jak v plzeňské studentské kavárně, tak pod barokní klenbou Lužického semináře.

Sychravé počasí za okny kontrastovalo s vřelou a neformální atmosférou obou večerů. U srdce zahřály i reakce návštěvníků. Etablovaný plzeňský básník Jan Sojka poklekl před organizátory večera na kolena, líbal jim ruce a děkoval za krásný večer. Herpetolog Ondřej Škach zase prohlásil, že nelituje toho, že vyměnil oslavu úspěšného odchovu zmije pavoučí v plzeňské ZOO, za lužickosrbský večer, neboť o zmijích ví všechno, ale o Lužici nevěděl doposud nic. Filolog Mikuláš Liptovský se nechal výkonem účinkujících dokonce strhnout ke slibu, že se na stará kolena pustí do studia sorabistiky. Studenty pražských uměleckých škol zase okouzlil Milan Hrabal natolik, že se zajímali o to, kdy bude mít v Lužickém semináři příští seminář o Lužici. Není divu, že se návštěvníci nechali vtáhnout do průběhu večera. Byl totiž úplně jiný, než obvykle literární večery bývají. Domašcyna s Hrabalem jsou na sebe mentálně navázaní a je na jejich vystoupení znát, že jsou sehraná dvojice. Kouba je pak skvěle doplňuje svými písněmi. Většina diváků slyšela asi poprvé dylanovku v lužické srbštině.  O pozitivních pocitech publika svědčí i ovace ve stoje, které následovaly po pražském večeru.

V době, kdy některé vlády vedou kulturní války proti vlastním občanům, tito se jim staví literaturou a radostí, kterou přináší umění slova. Je hezké vidět, když se lidé sejdou, aby vyslechli hlas malého národa a tím se o něco víc přiblížili ke břehům ostrova zapomenutých.

Martin Holý , Euskaldun
